title: Finite-field bounded constructible stratified generation
statement: Let $A$ be a finite field and $X$ a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of module sheaves over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ on small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathcal B_A(T)$ for the complexes whose cohomology vanishes outside a finite interval and is constructible [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]: there is a finite constructible locally closed stratification on which each cohomology sheaf is pro-étale locally constant with finite-dimensional $A$-module values. Every $P\in\mathcal B_A(X)$ can be obtained, up to isomorphism, from zero and finitely many objects $g_*j_!L$ by finitely many shifts and distinguished-triangle extensions. Here $S\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{g}X$ ranges over factorizations of constructible locally closed strata as an open immersion into the scheme-theoretic closure followed by its closed immersion [det-sf-flat-model-generation], and $L$ is a locally constant sheaf with finite-dimensional $A$-values on $S$ [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. A distinguished-triangle extension means the middle object of a distinguished triangle whose first and third objects are already constructed; no infinite sums or direct summands are required.

source.place: Lemmas 6.3.3 and 6.3.9, finite stratified dévissage in the proof of Lemma 6.7.13; degree-zero sheaf filtrations followed by the finite truncation tower.

proof.text: Work on the small-site skeleton in the common coefficient universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. For any ordinary $A_X$-module sheaf $F$, apply [lem-exc-constant-field-module-flat] with $\kappa=A$ and $J=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Its smallness hypothesis holds by this skeleton convention; use the ordinary commutative-ring and abelian-group sheafifications on the small site. Abelian sheafification exists by [lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification], and its locally-bijective criterion is [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective]. The associated constant ring is exactly the coefficient ring $A_X$ in the item. Hence $F$ is flat in the tensor-exactness sense. In particular this applies to each constructible cohomology sheaf of $P$.

source.place: Tags 03ER (definition-flat) and 08FC (lemma-flat-eq); Fields Tag 09FN (lemma-vector-space-is-free); application of the existing constant-field flatness theorem

proof.text: Let $F$ be any constructible $A_X$-module sheaf. Apply clauses (1) and (2) of [det-sf-flat-model-generation], using Step 1 for flatness. Its hypotheses are precisely a finite commutative ring and a Noetherian scheme on the ordinary pro-étale site; no finite-type or invertibility hypothesis is needed. Obtain finitely many locally closed strata $a_k:S_k\hookrightarrow X$, constructible because the underlying space of the Noetherian scheme $X$ is Noetherian, so every locally closed subset is constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset]; locally constant $L_k=F|_{S_k}$ with finite projective $A$-values, and a finite sheaf filtration $0=F_0\subset F_1\subset\cdots\subset F_m=F$ whose quotients are $a_{k!}L_k$. By that node's convention, $a_{k!}L_k=g_{k*}j_{k!}L_k$ for the open immersion into the scheme-theoretic closure followed by its closed immersion. A finitely generated module over the field $A$ is a finite-dimensional vector space, so these are generators of exactly the kind allowed here. We use the finite sheaf filtration in clause (2).

source.place: Clauses (1) and (2), with the ordinary pro-étale coefficient and locally closed extension conventions in the DAG statement

proof.text: For the filtration in Step 2, each short exact sequence $0\to F_{k-1}\to F_k\to g_{k*}j_{k!}L_k\to0$ gives the distinguished triangle $F_{k-1}[0]\to F_k[0]\to(g_{k*}j_{k!}L_k)[0]\to F_{k-1}[1]$ by [lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle]. Induct on $k=0,\ldots,m$: the initial object is zero, and at each successor the first and third terms have already been constructed, so the allowed middle-term extension constructs $F_k[0]$. The last object is $F[0]$. Thus every constructible sheaf in degree zero has a finite construction of the required form.

source.place: Tag 0152 (lemma-derived-canonical-delta-functor), applied to sheaves placed in degree zero

proof.text: Choose integers $a\le b$ with $H^q(P)=0$ for $q<a$ or $q>b$. Use the canonical truncations of [def-kun-truncations] and choose a complex representing $P$ in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The cohomology formulas for good truncations show that $\tau_{\le a-1}P$ is acyclic, hence isomorphic to zero, and that the inclusion $\tau_{\le b}P\to P$ is a quasi-isomorphism, hence an isomorphism in the derived category. These statements also cover an acyclic $P$, for which any interval can be chosen.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), with the cohomology formulas in Homology section-truncations

proof.text: For each integer $q=a,\ldots,b$, [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] gives $\tau_{\le q-1}P\to\tau_{\le q}P\to H^q(P)[-q]\to(\tau_{\le q-1}P)[1]$. Step 3 constructs $H^q(P)[0]$, and one further allowed shift operation, the automorphism $[-q]$ of the triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], constructs $H^q(P)[-q]$ (the complex with $H^q(P)$ in degree $q$ under the convention $(M[1])^r=M^{r+1}$). Starting at $\tau_{\le a-1}P\cong0$, induction over these $b-a+1$ triangles constructs the middle term $\tau_{\le q}P$ from the already constructed first and third terms. At $q=b$ this is $P$ up to the isomorphism of Step 4. Only finitely many $q$ occur, and each contributes finitely many strata and triangle steps. This gives one finite collection of the required generators and finitely many shifts and extensions. For the empty scheme or the zero object the construction may start and end at zero.

source.place: Tag 08J5 (remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle), second displayed triangle and finite induction

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q119-c91bb89b4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement is unchanged and true: it is the field-coefficient case of Bhatt-Scholze Lemmas 6.3.3 and 6.3.9 (pp. 45-46; perfect values equal finite-dimensional values over a field). It also holds in the small cases: zero, acyclic, empty X, one stratum, one cohomology degree. Step 1 meets every hypothesis of lem-exc-constant-field-module-flat: the V-small skeleton, lem-sfb-grothendieck-sheafification, and the local-bijectivity leaf. Step 2 meets the hypotheses of det-sf-flat-model-generation clauses (1)-(2): finite ring, Noetherian X, pro-etale site with ordinary constant-ring modules. That node's tower proof shows the 'iterated extension' is a finite filtration with quotients a_{k!}L_k = g_*j_!L_k. Step 3 is lem-sf-derived-ses-triangle (Stacks 0152) in the abelian category Mod(A_X). Step 4 follows from the good-truncation cohomology formulas of def-kun-truncations. Step 5 is lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle (Stacks 08J5), with the third term H^q[-q] and a correctly set-up induction from q=a to b. I accept all six declared tool_uses as generic tools. No duplicate exists: lem-sfb-stratified-tor-interval-devissage, lem-per-noetherian-ctf-flat-model, lem-per-constructible-extension-finite-stage and det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc all state something different. There are no new nodes and no SGA citations. FIX, two repairs: (C1/C4) clause (1) of the flat-model node gives only locally closed strata, while the item requires constructible ones. Step 2 now says X is a Noetherian space, so they are constructible, and cites def-weil-constructible-subset (Stacks 005L); it is added to uses and proof_deps. (C4) Step 5 said shifts of distinguished triangles are distinguished 'by def-weil-triangulated-category', which that definition does not state. I replaced this with one allowed shift [-q] applied to the constructed H^q(P)[0].; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
